name: Fit to plot
about: Finds the largest rectangle that fits an irregular plot inside its front, rear and side setbacks, at any angle, and draws it as the outer walls of the ground floor once you pick it.
useWhen: The owner wants the biggest rectangular building footprint a plot allows after its setbacks, as a start for the plan.

input.about: The plot: draw it on the canvas with the Site tool (P), or give its corners in the notes (x, y in metres or mm, in order), or attach a survey or a coordinates file. Say which side faces the road and the setbacks (front, rear, sides) if they are not set yet. Optional params: maxCoverage (0 to 1 of the plot), minSide (mm).

rules.text: Work in whole millimetres on the project's plan axes (x east, y north). The plot's corners go in order around it; edge k runs from corner k to corner k+1.
The front is the edge on the road; the rear is the edge facing away from it; every other edge is a side. Each keeps its setback; an edge may have its own (edges).
The footprint is a rectangle at any angle, wholly inside the plot and at least each edge's setback away from it. The outer face of the walls sits on it.
Only the owner's pick draws walls: one logged, undoable step.

steps.name: Read the plot
steps.outcome: The project has the plot from the brief: its corners in order, the front edge and the setbacks, set with set_site.

steps.name: Fit the largest rectangle
steps.outcome: The largest rectangles that fit inside the setbacks, at any angle: the best and up to two others.

steps.name: Pick the footprint
steps.question: Which footprint should become the outer walls of the ground floor? You can make it smaller and set the walls.

steps.name: Draw the outer walls
steps.outcome: The ground floor has a closed run of outer walls whose outer face sits on the footprint picked.

output.name: Footprint on the plot
output.about: The footprint picked, its area and share of the plot, and the walls drawn.
